dossier.public_summary: The dip looks shallow and flat but its depth changes by more than a factor of two between sectors and between individual transits, and three transits carry most of the signal. A star-like neighbour only 8.8 arcsec away could produce the dip with a ~48% eclipse, and difference images cannot confirm the target. This pattern matches a blended eclipsing binary plus noise, not a stable planet on the target M dwarf.

reasons.why: No on_target evidence despite 1 plausible neighbour within 1px (could_cause_within_1px 2, plausible_within_1px 1) and contratio 0.06304 - cannot confirm the dip is on the target vs a 0.4838 or 0.0316 eclipse on the 8.8 and 9.1 arcsec neighbours.
reasons.value: verdict inconclusive - no sector with a clear difference image (sectors_used null)

reasons.why: depths changed strongly between sectors and within the same source.

Not a calibration offset between products - the dip depth itself varies by a factor ~2 within QLP on the same star, expected for a background blended eclipsing binary whose dilution changes with aperture/sector rather than a transiting planet.
reasons.value: changes_within_a_source, QLP p_constant 0.00022078209456334388, depths 3550±1133 ppm (sect 33 SPOC), 3923±1434 ppm (sect 87 QLP), 10271±947 ppm (sect 98 QLP)

reasons.why: Individual transit depths are statistically inconsistent and 85.5% of the SNR (10.88, refit 10.69) comes from only 3 dips, inconsistent with a steady planet and expected if a few blended eclipses plus noise dominate.

Flat bottom and correct size/duration alone do not favour a planet because a diluted small-star eclipse also appears flat-bottomed, so the absence of warning signs (odd_even diff_sigma 0.7345, secondary snr 2.913) is outweighed by positive evidence for a neighbour/variability origin from the tools above; xgboost planet_rank 0.08 supports this false-positive appearance.
